rationale: Phase 0 of the path to the dinner table (LEARNING-SYSTEM.md §5): get the ear and the mouth right BEFORE habits set. Six contrasts trip up every learner of city Palestinian. Realizations match pipeline/subdialect.py (urban: ق→ء, ث→t, ذ→d, emphatics preserved) — the same model the app's audio voice uses.
provenance_note: Articulation notes are curated linguistic description (accurate, but written by us, not a lexicon). Example words are everyday Palestinian; romanization follows the app's urban CAPHI realization. Audio, when generated, is synthesized in the pinned voice — a reference, not a native recording; the gutturals ع/ح and the emphatics are exactly where TTS is least reliable, so trust the articulation note over the clip for those.

lessons.en: ق — the qaf that becomes a catch
lessons.tip: In city speech (Jerusalem, Ramallah, Nablus) the letter ق is a GLOTTAL STOP — the little catch in the middle of “uh-oh”. Not a hard “q”, not a “k”. So قهوة is “ˈahwe” and قلب is “ˈalb”. (Villages keep a hard “k” for ق — that’s the Wadi Ara sound.)

lessons.en: ع — the sound English doesn't have
lessons.tip: ع (ʿayn) is a tightening deep in the throat — squeeze as if starting a strained “aaah”, then release into the vowel. It is NOT a vowel and NOT the soft catch of a hamza (أ). Feel the throat close for عم (ʿam) but stay open for أم (umm).

lessons.en: ح خ ه — three throat sounds
lessons.tip: ه is a plain English “h”. ح is a strong WHISPERED h from deep in the throat — breathe hard through a tight throat, no rasp. خ is a RASP — like clearing your throat, the “ch” in Scottish “loch”. The trio حال / خال / هال are three different words.

lessons.en: ط ص ض ظ — the heavy letters
lessons.tip: Emphatics are said with the tongue pulled BACK and the mouth darker and rounder — they bend the vowel next to them toward “ah/oh”. Say تين (tiin, figs) then طين (Tiin, mud) and feel the second one drop and darken. Same for سار / صار.

lessons.en: ث ذ — the 'th' sounds city speech drops
lessons.tip: Standard Arabic ث (as in “think”) and ذ (as in “this”) collapse to STOPS in city Palestinian: ث → t, ذ → d. So ثلاثة is “tlaate”, ذهب is “dahab”, هذا is “haada”. (Village and bedouin speech keep the th / dh.)

lessons.en: ē, ō, and long vs short
lessons.tip: Palestinian has ē and ō where standard Arabic has “ay” and “aw”: بيت is “bēt” (not bayt), يوم is “yōm”. And vowel LENGTH changes the word: عم (ʿam, the ‘-ing’ marker) vs عام (ʿaam, year). Hold the long vowels long.
